 Democratic gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra addresses the attendees at a campaign event for Democratic Assembly candidate Clarissa Cervantes at UDW Union Hall in Riverside on Friday, Oct. 2, 2026 in Riverside. (Photo by Milka Soko, Contributing Photographer)
 By Larry Wilson | lwilson@scng.com PUBLISHED: October 30, 2026 at 11:42 AM PDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... When the now-famous “Death” issue of the National Lampoon arrived in the mail  — the one with the cover of a man holding a pistol to a pup’s head, with the headline, “If you don’t buy this magazine, we’ll kill this dog”  — I tore it open.
 Inside was a Playboy parody, “Playdead.” Dan Blocker, Hoss on “Bonanza,” had recently died. In a takedown of the monthly Playboy Interview, a journalist was sent to interview the deceased. The magazine asked a number of questions  — “How much of the show’s success would you say is attributable to your gun vis a vis your brother’s and father’s guns?” — and the answer was always the same: “Blocker:” followed by a couple of inches of white space on the page.
 Blocker was dead. Dead men tell no tales.
 Xavier Becerra is not dead. In fact, he is the next governor of California, our home. How cool is that? If I were a politician I’d be jumping for joy and telling everyone how happy I was.
 But from the next governor himself, we don’t know how cool it is. Becerra is not talking. Not to me — his people have repeatedly declined to make him available for a brief chat about the campaign for this column — but really not to anyone in the press.
 His campaign would say that the candidate prefers to speak directly to voters at community events around the Golden State. Oh, sure. All those giant Becerra rallies! They’re everywhere.
 I had asked the campaign for an interview before, right after Becerra became the Democratic front-runner after the Eric Swalwell implosion. Crickets.
 But about a month ago, with Election Day fast approaching, I tried again.
 Q: “Hi Sara — it’s Larry Wilson, deputy Opinion editor for the Southern California News Group. Could I please interview Mr. Becerra for my Sunday column? With many thanks, Larry”
 A: “Hi Lawrence. Thanks for your request. Can you provide some more information, how long are you requesting, assuming a phone call is OK and if there is a specific topic you would like to cover? Also, what your deadline is for this interview? Thanks.”
 Q: “Hi Sara  — thanks much. I would like to ask the (future) governor about his plans for his first term, what the relationship he hopes to establish with the Legislature is, what the best way toward housing affordability is, how he would work with the mayors and supervisors to decrease homelessness, whether there is a divide between north and south and rural and coastal California and their needs and how best to keep the billionaires here as they face economic pressures to leave. Half an hour on the phone would be great. Cheers, Larry”
 A: “Hi Larry — thanks for your interest in interviewing Secretary Becerra. Unfortunately, due to his schedule demands at this point  we can’t schedule this interview, but we can make sure you are on our distribution list so you can potentially attend an event and ask him some questions during the gaggle.”

 Which Athenian legacy will Americans carry on in the midterms? 
 Geez, were my sofballs too hard? Are there really any gaggles? I wouldn’t know, as I was never put on any distribution list about any events, if there are such. I went through a similar exchange with another comms staffer, who ended up just ghosting me.
 I get the strategy, I suppose, that since Becerra’s going to beat Steve Hilton at the polls on Tuesday anyway, what’s the use of gabbing with the press, other than a potential gaffe?
 But that’s a sick and cynical approach to politics. Hey, eight years ago, Gavin Newsom came in person for a long visit with the editorial board of the Orange County Register, knowing he had no chance of landing its endorsement. But he came, and he engaged.
 I find it really depressing and actually worrisome for California that our next governor declines to engage.
 Larry Wilson is on the Southern California News Group editorial board. lwilson@scng.com.
